variants.value: tag=r2p12p5pct; shift 12.5% R0 mass (4707 dots) range_front->piedmont; fixed count 37654; added d_cat>=3px

mechanism_card.hypothesis: Shifting 12.5% of R0 mass (4,707 dots) out of high-relief Range-front/horst interiors (T3) into Piedmont/bajada aprons (T2) trims false-positive erosional bedrock ridges while densifying H19-5 coverage across range-bounding synthetic splays, relay ramps, and step-over zones without placing mass onto flat, thickly buried playa floors.
mechanism_card.mechanism: Landform relief terciles are computed from `det_elev` (0.85 percentile weight) and 3 km Gaussian-smoothed `det_elev_slope` (0.15 percentile weight). R0 allocates 37.95% of dots to T3 vs 29.19% of known USGS/INGENIOUS faults because bare bedrock topography excites ridge detectors. Greedily dropping the 4,707 lowest-exclusive-credit R0 dots in T3 and greedily adding the 4,707 highest-marginal-credit H19-5 ridge pixels in T2 (all with d_cat >= 3.0 px) holds count fixed at 37,654 while tightening kernel coverage along piedmont fault corridors where 400 m GeoDAWN flight-line spacing leaves ~150-300 m lateral position uncertainty.
mechanism_card.non_fault_confounder: Coalescing alluvial-fan incised channels, terrace risers, Lake Lahontan highstand shorelines, and piedmont road/pipeline magnetic anomalies can mimic piedmont fault lineaments in H19-5.

mechanism_card.non_fault_confounder: Pleistocene pluvial shoreline berms (Lake Lahontan), axial fluvial channels, buried basaltic sills/flows, and valley-floor cultural infrastructure (railways/powerlines) produce non-fault magnetic/topographic ridges in T1.

prior_session_variants.value: d_cat<=3.5px; fixed-count FIFO-BFS H19-5 refill; min d_cat>3.5px

mechanism_card.hypothesis: At d_cat<=3.5 px, R0's near-catalogue flank dots contain more false-positive mass than new-fault credit; replacing that collar with the same lineage's next-ranked ridge pixels should improve DTI without changing the emitted mass.
mechanism_card.mechanism: Known catalogue pixels are masked pixel-exactly, while a nearby new fault remains scoreable; the PRUNE edit tests whether the empirical 2.0 px collar is too narrow. It drops every parent dot inside the specified radius and replaces the exact count from the H19-5 support, using its recovered FIFO-BFS thinning order, only where d_cat is strictly outside the new collar.
mechanism_card.non_fault_confounder: H19-5's next-priority pixels may be ridges from lithologic contacts, drainage margins, or topographic lineaments rather than faults; new-fault truth may also cluster beside known traces.
mechanism_card.predicted_live_change: +0.002 DTI (MODEL; plausible interval -0.010 to +0.010; not a score)
mechanism_card.falsifier: A paired, same-week live receipt against R0 with Δ<=-0.010 falsifies the proposed positive collar effect for this cutoff/refill policy. Any |Δ|<0.010 is no evidence under the session rule.
mechanism_card.structural_geologist_note: Interpret this as a positional-uncertainty/collar experiment, not as a claim that faults do not continue near mapped traces. Review both removed flanks and FIFO-ranked refill ridges on geology.
